To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The distribution of lymphocyte subsets in the large intestine of patients with AIDS was different from that in controls.
intestinal T cells in AIDS patients have an activated and differentiated phenotype, but a decreased CD4/CD8 ratio, which may contribute specifically to the secondary infections observed in the gut.
In intestinal biopsies of HIV‐infactory patients, the number of CD4 T cells is reduced, whereas the number of CD8 T ceils is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of T lymphocytes in the pathogenesis of HIV infection and AIDS.
the role of the intestinal immune system in HIV infection and the development of AIDS.
the study of the immunopathology of AIDS and the mechanisms of immune dysfunction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intestinal immune response to HIV is characterized by a selective impairment of CD4 T cells.
the gut is not a sanctuary site, and the gut is not an immune‐privileged site.
HIV‐1‐infected individuals have a reduced number of intestinal CD4 T ceils and that the CD4 T cells which remain are in a state of activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in AIDS patients the CD4 T cell population is reduced and CD8 cytotoxic T cell population is increased in the intestinal lamina propria.
the CD8 T cell response in the intestine is increased in HIV‐infected persons.

HIV‐induced alterations in the distribution, activation, differentiation and functional status of intestinal T cells may contribute to the development of secondary infections and malignancy of the gut in AIDS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant increase in the number of CD8 cells in the large intestine, but the CD4 cells are significantly reduced.
the gut mucosal immune system is profoundly affected by HIV infection, and this has important consequences for the development of secondary infections and malignancy.
the gut is a major reservoir for HIV infection.
